sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: GUIDANCE REMAINS CONSISTENT SHOWING THE DEVELOPMENT OF QUASI-ZONAL MID-UPPER LEVEL FLOW REGIME ACROSS THE NRN U.S. AS THE UPPER TROUGH OVER THE ERN STATES SHIFTS SLOWLY EWD AND A PROGRESSIVE TROUGH TRACKS FROM THE NRN INTERMOUNTAIN WEST TO THE NRN PLAINS. THE NRN EXTENT OF THE UPPER RIDGE...CURRENTLY RESIDING OVER THE NRN HIGH PLAINS...WILL SHIFT E TOWARD THE UPPER MS VALLEY WITH THE APPROACH OF THE UPSTREAM TROUGH. THIS WILL RESULT IN WEAK HEIGHT FALLS ACROSS THE NRN/CENTRAL PLAINS. IN THE LOW LEVELS...A SURFACE LOW IS EXPECTED TO DEEPEN OVER ERN CO TODAY...AND THEN SHIFT EWD INTO WRN KS TONIGHT. MEANWHILE...AN E-W BOUNDARY SHOULD BECOME BETTER DEFINED FROM NRN KS TO NRN MO THIS FORECAST PERIOD. THE KS PORTION MAY BE REINFORCED BY CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW ASSOCIATED WITH CURRENT ONGOING TSTMS IN THE CENTRAL PLAINS AND/OR ANY ADDITIONAL TSTM COMPLEXES THAT COULD DEVELOP OVER NEB PRIOR TO THE START OF THE DAY 1 PERIOD. FARTHER W...AN ENE-WSW ORIENTED FRONT IS EXPECTED TO MOVE SWD INTO NRN UT AND SRN WY LATE THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING.

sections.title: SRN AND CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS EWD TO SRN IA/NRN MO
sections.text: TSTMS ARE EXPECTED TO BE ONGOING AT 12Z TODAY ACROSS PARTS OF THE CENTRAL PLAINS WITHIN WAA REGIME ALONG NOSE OF NOCTURNAL SSWLY LLJ. SOME OF THIS EARLY MORNING ACTIVITY MAY BE SEVERE GIVEN ERN EXTENT OF STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES...MODERATE INSTABILITY AND STRONG EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR. EVENTUAL WEAKENING OF THE LLJ THIS MORNING SHOULD SUPPORT A DECREASING TREND IN STORM INTENSITY/COVERAGE WITH THIS ONGOING ACTIVITY SHIFTING E/SEWD ACROSS THE ERN PORTION OF THE CENTRAL PLAINS AND MIDDLE-LOWER MO VALLEY. THE ELEVATED MIXED LAYER IS EXPECTED TO PROGRESS FARTHER ENEWD ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS TODAY AND SHOULD EFFECTIVELY CAP MUCH OF THIS REGION FROM HAVING AFTERNOON TSTM DEVELOPMENT. MEANWHILE...NEW TSTM DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED TO OCCUR THIS AFTERNOON FARTHER TO THE W OVER ERN CO/SERN WY WITHIN ELY MOIST UPSLOPE FLOW REGIME N OF THE CO SURFACE LOW. A MODERATE-VERY UNSTABLE AIR MASS /MLCAPE 2000-3000 J PER KG/ AND 50 KT OF EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR INDICATE THESE STORMS SHOULD QUICKLY BECOME SUPERCELLS WITH AN ATTENDANT THREAT FOR ISOLATED TORNADOES... HAIL...SOME VERY LARGE...AND DAMAGING WINDS. A BROAD SSWLY LLJ IS EXPECTED TO REDEVELOP FROM W TX/OK INTO KS THIS EVENING WITH SPEEDS INCREA

sections.title: NRN UT TO SRN WY
sections.text: SLIGHT RISK HAS BEEN INTRODUCED FROM SRN WY/NWRN CO INTO NRN UT. SURFACE DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 40S-LOWER 50S...SURFACE HEATING AND NRN EXTENT OF STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES ARE EXPECTED TO RESULT IN MLCAPE VALUES UP TO 1000 J/KG BY THIS AFTERNOON. TSTMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP ALONG AND AHEAD OF THE SWD MOVING BAROCLINIC ZONE. THIS ACTIVITY HAS THE POTENTIAL TO BE SEVERE INTO THE EVENING...GIVEN THE AVAILABLE INSTABILITY AND 50 KT OF EFFECTIVE SHEAR.

sections.title: NM
sections.text: PRIMARILY DIURNAL TSTMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP THIS AFTERNOON ALONG THE HIGHER TERRAIN AND WITHIN LOW LEVEL CONVERGENCE ZONE EXTENDING GENERALLY N-S THROUGH CENTRAL NM. THIS ACTIVITY WILL BE SUPPORTED BY MODERATE INSTABILITY AND STEEP LAPSE RATES. WEAK DEEP LAYER SHEAR SUGGESTS ACTIVITY WILL BE PULSE AND OUTFLOW DOMINANT WITH ISOLATED DAMAGING WINDS THE PRIMARY THREAT. ..PETERS/SMITH.. 06/07/2010

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: FAIRLY ZONAL FLOW WILL PREVAIL OVER THE LWR 48 THIS PERIOD...IN WAKE OF AMPLIFIED TROUGH SLOWLY EXITING THE NERN STATES. LOW AMPLITUDE SHORTWAVE IMPULSE NOW OVER ORE WILL REACH THE NRN RCKYS THIS EVE...BEFORE CONTINUING E TO THE NRN HI PLNS EARLY TUE. OTHERWISE...UPR RIDGE WILL LINGER OVER THE SRN RCKYS/SRN HI PLNS...WHILE WEAK UPR LOW PERSISTS OVER S TX. AT LWR LVLS...LEE LOW EXPECTED TO SLOWLY DEEPEN OVER ERN CO TODAY...WHILE ASSOCIATED FRONTAL ZONE EXTENDING ESE INTO CNTRL KS BECOMES BETTER DEFINED. THE LOW SHOULD BEGIN TO MOVE E/NE ACROSS NRN KS TONIGHT AS DEVELOPING COLD FRONT...INITIALLY OVER WY/UT...ACCELERATES S INTO CO.

sections.title: CNTRL HI PLNS TO LWR MO VLY THIS AFTN/TONIGHT
sections.text: SCTD HIGH-BASED AND/OR ELEVATED TSTMS WITH A THREAT FOR SVR HAIL LIKELY WILL PERSIST FOR SEVERAL MORE HOURS IN WAA AREA ON EDGE OF EML...FROM NE CO/SE WY EWD INTO CNTRL NEB/NRN KS. A FEW ELEVATED STORMS ALSO MAY PERSIST OVER SW KS AND THE OK/NRN TX PANHANDLES ...IN WAKE OF WEAKENING OVERNIGHT MCS NOW IN NE OK. OTHERWISE...EML SPREADING E FROM THE SRN/CNTRL PLATEAU AHEAD OF ORE UPR IMPULSE SHOULD EFFECTIVELY CAP MUCH OF THE CNTRL PLNS FROM AFTN TSTM DEVELOPMENT. AFTN STORMS SHOULD...HOWEVER...FORM IN UPSLOPE FLOW OVER NE CO...ERN WY...AND WRN NEB...N OF ERN CO SFC LOW. STRONG INSTABILITY /SBCAPE TO 3000 J PER KG/ WILL EXIST...REFLECTING...IN PART...SFC DEWPOINTS IN THE 60S F. COUPLED WITH 50 KT DEEP SHEAR ON SRN EDGE OF THE WLYS...THE STORMS SHOULD QUICKLY BECOME SUPERCELLS WITH VERY LARGE HAIL AND DMGG WIND. APPRECIABLE LOW-LVL DIRECTIONAL SHEAR ALSO WILL BE FAVORABLE FOR TORNADOES. CONTINUED EWD MOVEMENT OF ORE IMPULSE...AND NIGHTFALL...WILL FOSTER CONSIDERABLE STRENGTHENING AND BROADENING OF SSWLY LLJ OVER THE CNTRL PLNS TONIGHT/EARLY TUE. ASSOCIATED WAA ATOP AFOREMENTIONED FRONTAL ZONE SHOULD SUPPORT EWD DEVELOPMENT OF THE WY/NE CO/WRN NEB STORMS...AND/OR NEW DEVELOPMENT...OVER

sections.title: NRN UT/SRN WY/NW CO THIS AFTN/EVE
sections.text: ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH APPROACH OF ORE UPR IMPULSE WILL ENHANCE DIURNAL DESTABILIZATION OVER SRN WY...NRN UT...AND NW CO TODAY. WHILE MOISTURE WILL BE LIMITED BY CNTRL/ERN U.S. STANDARDS... SUFFICIENT MOISTURE SHOULD BE PRESENT TO SUPPORT STRONG STORM DEVELOPMENT ALONG STRENGTHENING COLD FRONT AS SBCAPE INCREASES TO AOA 500 J/KG. GIVEN 40-50 KT DEEP WSWLY SHEAR AND STEEP LOW TO MID LVL LAPSE RATES...THE STORMS MAY YIELD HIGH WIND AND MARGINALLY SVR HAIL.

sections.title: NM THIS AFTN/EVE
sections.text: ANOTHER ROUND OF STRONG AFTN/EVE PULSE STORMS EXPECTED OVER THE NM REGION TODAY...AS TERRAIN CIRCULATIONS LIFT MOISTURE TRAPPED BENEATH UPR ANTICYCLONE. COMBINATION OF MODERATE INSTABILITY AND STEEP LOW LVL LAPSE RATES WITH WEAK SHEAR SUGGESTS POTENTIAL FOR A FEW OUTFLOW-DOMINANT STORMS WITH DMGG WIND. ..CORFIDI/STOPPKOTTE.. 06/07/2010

sections.title: CENTRAL/SRN HIGH PLAINS EWD INTO THE LOWER MO VALLEY
sections.text: SHORT TERM MESOSCALE MODELS WERE POOR IN FORECASTING EVENTUAL EVOLUTION OF ELEVATED THUNDERSTORMS THIS MORNING FROM THE NERN TX PANHANDLE NWD INTO CENTRAL NEB. 700-800 MB WLY WARM ADVECTION FEEDING OVER OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM OVERNIGHT CONVECTION APPEARED TO BE THE SOURCE FOR CONVECTION. ISOLATED SEVERE HAIL AND EVEN SOME WIND DAMAGE WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH STORMS THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS...ESPECIALLY SMALL CLUSTER EAST OF DDC...REFERENCE WW 279. UNLESS COMPLEX CAN BE MAINTAINED SEWD INTO OK...STORMS SHOULD GRADUALLY DECREASE AS WARM ADVECTION SLOWLY SHIFTS EWD INTO A LESS UNSTABLE ELEVATED ENVIRONMENT. ALSO DUE TO MORNING CONVECTION...HAVE ADDED SLIGHT RISK FROM WRN KS SWD INTO THE OK/TX PANHANDLES. OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES IN THESE AREAS MAY PROVIDE SUFFICIENT CONVERGENCE FOR STORMS TO DEVELOP THIS AFTERNOON WITH HEATING. ALTHOUGH THE DEEP LAYER SHEAR WILL NOT BE PARTICULARLY STRONG...ESPECIALLY IN THE TX PANHANDLE... VERY STEEP MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES/INSTABILITY WILL EXIST ACROSS THE AREA. THE AMOUNT OF INSTABILITY FAVORS HAIL...AND THE LARGE HIGH BASED CAPE WITH EXPECTED 25-30 DEGREE T/TD SPREADS SUPPORT DAMAGING WINDS. FURTHER NORTH...THE BOUNDARY LAYER IS QUITE COOL AND WIDESPREAD EXTE

sections.text: ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH NRN ROCKIES IMPULSE WILL ENHANCE DIURNAL DESTABILIZATION OVER SRN WY...NRN UT...AND NW CO THIS AFTERNOON. SUFFICIENT MOISTURE SHOULD BE PRESENT TO SUPPORT STRONG STORM DEVELOPMENT ALONG STRENGTHENING COLD FRONT AS SBCAPE INCREASES TO AOA 500 J/KG. GIVEN 40-50 KT DEEP WSWLY SHEAR AND STEEP LOW TO MID LVL LAPSE RATES...THE STORMS MAY YIELD A FEW HIGH WIND AND MARGINALLY SVR HAIL REPORTS. ..IMY/JEWELL.. 06/07/2010

sections.title: CNTRL AND SRN PLAINS AREA
sections.text: PRIMARY ZONE OF ROBUST CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED THIS EVENING ACROSS THE CNTRL PLAINS WHERE STRENGTHENING LOW LEVEL JET WILL AUGMENT LIFT AND THETA-E ADVECTION IN VICINITY DEEPER BAROCLINIC ZONE. INITIAL STORMS SHOULD DEVELOP OVER THE HIGH PLAINS OF WY AND CO AS CAP CONTINUES TO WEAKEN AND WHERE VISIBLE IMAGERY SHOW CUMULUS INCREASING OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN. STORMS WILL EVENTUALLY DEVELOP EWD...LIKELY EVOLVING INTO ONE OR MORE MCSS. EFFECTIVE VERTICAL SHEAR IN THIS REGION WILL SUPPORT ORGANIZED STORMS INCLUDING SUPERCELLS AND BOWING STRUCTURES WITH DAMAGING WIND AND LARGE HAIL THE MAIN THREATS. ISOLATED TORNADOES WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE...MAINLY OVER THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS THIS EVENING. SEVERE THREAT OVER THE SRN PLAINS IS STILL SOMEWHAT UNCERTAIN AND CONDITIONAL DUE TO CONCERNS REGARDING EXTENT OF CONVECTIVE INITIATION. AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WAS INDICATED SURGING SWD THROUGH WRN OK INTO THE NERN TX PANHANDLE. ANOTHER OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WAS INDICATED FROM WRN TN SWWD THROUGH SRN AR THEN NWWD INTO SWRN OK. POTENTIAL STILL EXISTS FOR STORMS TO DEVELOP ALONG THE SWD SURGING OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM WRN OK INTO THE TX PANHANDLE AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER CONTINUES TO WARM. FLOW ALOFT IS WEA

sections.title: SERN WY/NERN CO THROUGH NEB/NRN KS TO WRN/SRN IA AND NRN MO
sections.text: EARLY EVENING SURFACE ANALYSIS SHOWED A BAROCLINIC ZONE EXTENDING ESEWD FROM A SURFACE LOW IN SERN WY THROUGH CENTRAL/SRN NEB TO SRN IA. A VERY MOIST AIR MASS HAS RETURNED NWD INTO WRN AND SRN NEB WITH SURFACE DEWPOINTS IN THE MID-UPPER 60S. THIS MOISTENING IS EVIDENT WHEN COMPARING THE 18Z AND 00Z LBF SOUNDINGS...WITH THE LATTER SOUNDING SHOWING STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES /AROUND 8 C PER KM/ HAVE BEEN MAINTAINED ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS. THIS IS RESULTING IN MODERATE INSTABILITY AVAILABLE FOR ADDITIONAL TSTM DEVELOPMENT THROUGH THE EVENING INTO THE OVERNIGHT PERIOD. RADAR MOSAICS AND COOLING CLOUD TOPS PER IR SATELLITE IMAGERY INDICATED A STRONG-SEVERE TSTM COMPLEX EVOLVING OVER EXTREME SERN WY INTO THE NEB PANHANDLE. FORCING FOR ASCENT IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE ACROSS THE BAROCLINIC ZONE THIS FORECAST PERIOD AS THE ENTRANCE REGION OF A 70 KT WSWLY MIDLEVEL JET SPREADS EWD ACROSS NEB AND LOW LEVEL WAA INCREASES SUBSTANTIALLY ACROSS THIS SAME REGION AS A NOCTURNAL SLY LLJ STRENGTHENS TO 50 KT INTO THE CENTRAL PLAINS. TORNADO THREAT WILL CONTINUE ACROSS EXTREME SERN WY INTO WRN NEB/NERN CO...GIVEN SELY SURFACE WINDS ENHANCING LOW LEVEL SHEAR /EFFECTIVE SRH 200-300 M2 PER S2 PER OBJEC

sections.title: ERN CO
sections.text: A FEW ORGANIZED STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE THIS EVENING ACROSS ERN CO...GIVEN RESIDUAL MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY AND EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 40-50 KT. FURTHER STABILIZATION OF THE BOUNDARY LAYER WITH THE ONSET OF SURFACE COOLING SHOULD RESULT IN ACTIVITY WANING BY LATE EVENING.

sections.title: CENTRAL/ERN UT TO NWRN CO/SRN WY
sections.text: A CORRIDOR OF MARGINAL INSTABILITY REMAINING AHEAD OF A FRONT ADVANCING SWD INTO CENTRAL/ERN UT...NRN CO AND SRN WY THIS EVENING WILL SUPPORT A FEW ADDITIONAL STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS. EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR UP TO 50 KT SUGGESTS ACTIVITY WILL REMAIN CAPABLE OF BEING ORGANIZED WITH A THREAT FOR HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. ..PETERS.. 06/08/2010
